newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says new Zaire PM nomination hopeful sign.
newsitem.headline: France says new Zaire PM nomination hopeful sign.

text.p: France expressed hope on Thursday that the appointment of opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi as Zairean prime minister would lead to fruitful negotiations with rebels fighting to topple ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Mobutu agreed on Wednesday to name Tshisekedi, hitherto an arch-foe, to the post from which he was sacked in 1993. Parliament had nominated Tshisekedi the previous day.
"We have noted the appointment of Etienne Tshisekedi as the new head of the Zairean government," the French Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Thursday.
"This should create a propitious climate for intra-Zairean negotiations which are to begin at the end of the week in South Africa," the statement said.
A delegation from rebel forces based in eastern Zaire and led by Laurent Kabila is due to go to South Africa for the first negotiations with representatives of Zaire's government.
The rebel delegation was expected to leave eastern Zaire on Thursday, rebel officials said.
Mobutu has named a seven-member commission to attend the weekend negotiations.
France also expressed concern on Thursday over the situation of refugees displaced by the fighting in eastern Zaire and said it was working with its western partners to find a way to help them.

"The humanitarian situation of the refugees and displaced people continues to be very worrying. We have increased our efforts with all those who could have an influence on the concerned parties," the ministry's statement said.
